## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API (63/13)

## Structure and components

- [statement] RPI orders must be Post-Only, are guaranteed by the matching engine to match only Retail Taker orders, have the lowest execution priority at their price level, rest until cancelled, and are placed via the New Order endpoint with `instruction="RPI"`. The UI book can appear crossed because of RPI orders, while the API orderbook never contains them. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/rpi · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://members.delphidigital.io/reports/paradex-reimagining-on-chain-markets-from-first-principles
- [statement] Order signing is computationally expensive. Paradex's best-practices page quotes 0.4ms (C++) and 0.2ms (Rust) average signing latency and advises pre-signing static order components, using the optional `market` parameter on cancel-by-client-id, and using the `bbo.{market_symbol}` WebSocket channel for price-only strategies. The Python SDK paradex-py supports L1 + L2 authentication. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/api-best-practices · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-py

## How it works

- [statement] Paradex says it funds zero retail fees from RPI maker flow: professional makers post RPI orders visible in the UI but hidden from the API, which match only against retail takers, and pay 0.5 bps on RPI fills; the launch blog also said high-frequency API takers pay 2 bps and that toxicity-based fees would follow. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-09-16) — https://www.paradex.trade/blog/introducing-zero-fee-perps · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://members.delphidigital.io/reports/paradex-reimagining-on-chain-markets-from-first-principles
- [statement] The documented way to mark API orders as Retail changed: one docs commit told API users to include the `INTERACTIVE` flag when submitting orders; a later commit removed that section; and another re-added it with corrected instructions to request a JWT token with the `token_usage=interactive` query parameter. Code written from the INTERACTIVE-flag instructions may be obsolete. A comment thread under Delphi's report, asked how Paradex determines who is retail, still answered "it's ui (retail) and api (HFTs/MMs)". (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/f3d99c5070d615a82da9984188173b2da870663d · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/1bd62650e0df0c28bb082ae6c83e8b9d4cb937ac, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles, https://members.delphidigital.io/reports/paradex-reimagining-on-chain-markets-from-first-principles
- [statement] Incident (official account): on Jan 19 a planned 30-minute database upgrade hit a race condition during a service restart, a corrupted state was persisted and published to Paradex Chain, and some markets reset the funding index to 0, creating abnormal funding PnL that triggered liquidations. Paradex rolled the chain back to block 1604710 (04:27:54 UTC), cancelled all open orders except TP/SL orders, and saw additional liquidations primarily on PAXG when aggressive orders skewed the mark price during the post-only period. Within 24 hours it refunded $650,000 across 200 accounts from the Liquidator Vault, called this Paradex Chain's first rollback, and added restart-procedure, data-validation, scale-up-process and post-only price-band safeguards. (high confidence) — https://x.com/paradex/status/2014616141508051376 · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://www.tradingview.com/news/cointelegraph:7fc5cadc0094b:0-paradex-refunds-650k-to-200-users-after-maintenance-bug-triggers-liquidations/, https://status.paradex.trade/posts/details/PVQ05Y4, https://www.dlnews.com/articles/defi/paradex-announces-rollback-after-perp-exchange-users-report-mass-liquidations/
- [statement] Paradex docs described the Retail API switch inconsistently. One docs commit (message: "Split into Trading Fees and Trader Profiles pages, add retail API identification docs") told API users to include the `INTERACTIVE` flag when submitting orders. A commit dated Wed, 11 Mar 2026 removed that section ("Remove INTERACTIVE token section for retail trading"). A later commit re-added it with "corrected instructions" that request a JWT token with the `token_usage=interactive` query parameter via POST /v1/auth?token_usage=interactive. (high confidence) — https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/f3d99c5070d615a82da9984188173b2da870663d · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/b30974537801baa890508b7eda10e79fa654c5f0, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/1bd62650e0df0c28bb082ae6c83e8b9d4cb937ac, https://api.prod.paradex.trade/swagger/doc.json, https://docs.paradex.trade/api/prod/auth/get-jwt

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] To audit which lane a fill got, read the `flags` array on fills from List Fills: `fastfill` marks a fill that qualified for the FastFills discount of 30%. The discounted fee amount is in the fill's `fee` field. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://api.prod.paradex.trade/swagger/doc.json · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/fastfills

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Paradex docs state that Retail takers and makers pay 0% fees on Perps, Spot and Options, and RFQ takers pay 0% on all products; the 'Zero Fee Perps' program went live on Mainnet in a blog post dated September 16, 2025, covering 100+ perps on web and mobile. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://www.paradex.trade/blog/introducing-zero-fee-perps
- [statement] Retail orders carry a 300ms speed bump on both submission and cancellation, and limits of 3 orders / sec, 30 orders / min, 300 orders / hr and 1,000 orders / 24 hrs. In exchange they get Retail fees, queue priority at each price level and access to RPI liquidity. The RPI page says Retail Taker orders face rate limits between 267-575x lower than standard API limits. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/rpi
- [statement] Pro taker fees are volume-tiered on 14D volume (Pro 0 = 0.045% down to Pro 4 at ≥ 25M = 0.035%), reduced by additive discounts (stake $DIME up to 30%, pay fees in $DIME 40% during initial rollout, FastFills 30%), with a floor of 1.75 bps (0.0175%). Pro maker is a flat 0.005% per the docs. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API
- [statement] FastFills: an API order that matches a passive Retail order gets an automatic 30% fee discount, flagged `fastfill` in List Fills `flags`. The orderbook endpoint exposes `best_bid_interactive`, `best_ask_interactive`, `best_bid_api` and `best_ask_api` sizes, and UI orders have queue priority at each price level. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/fastfills · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles
- [statement] Paradex advertises 0% maker and 0% taker fees for Retail orders on Perps, Spot and Options, and 0% for RFQ takers on every product. It launched 'Zero Fee Perps' on mainnet for retail on 100+ perps across web and mobile in a post dated September 16, 2025. Paradex's live fee API agrees with the docs: GET /v1/system/volume-tiers returned maker 0 and taker 0 for every Retail tier, VIP 0 through VIP 6. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://www.paradex.trade/blog/introducing-zero-fee-perps, https://api.prod.paradex.trade/v1/system/volume-tiers
- [statement] Retail orders pay for the zero fee with friction: a 300ms speed bump on both order submission and cancellation, and limits of 3 orders / sec, 30 orders / min, 300 orders / hr and 1,000 orders / 24 hrs. Pro orders have no speed bump and 800 orders / sec and 17,250 orders / min. In return Retail gets fee eligibility, queue priority at each price level and access to RPI liquidity. The submission speed bump was 500ms until a docs commit with the message 'update speedbump values' cut it to 300ms; the Retail rate limits appear unchanged in that commit. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/53388a63ab02b88ef757c742fa4bb9edea5504ce, https://www.hyperfolio.fun/en/blog/hyperliquid-vs-paradex-comparison
- [statement] The Pro maker fee has moved repeatedly. Paradex announced Pro maker 0% effective March 25, 2026; the docs then added a flat 0.003% (0.3 bps) effective July 3 at 12:00 SGT; and by 2026-11 the docs raised it to a flat 0.5 bps (0.005%). A practitioner who tracked it described the path as "a decaying incentive on a schedule" and advised re-reading the fee schedule the day before funding anything. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/8b83f586ea47ec8466e3bba82c26987f1872d974 · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/276781da90822aa3ec1add322005d8957825b087, https://x.com/paradex/status/2036439864443543880, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/332fbc281b595c664ac5bd5b442517cdf267d632, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/226f03c3eec1eb2404c8749fe5cf469b6a8b1bbe
- [statement] Retail was not always zero in 2026. Paradex announced Retail taker 0.0075% and Pro maker 0% effective March 25, 2026 at 1:00 PM SGT (5:00 UTC); the docs then listed Retail VIP tiers (VIP 0 (Default) taker 0.024% down to VIP 6 at 0.01%, with lower volume thresholds for holders of two named NFTs, MoneyBadgers and ShizoPunks) after a one-week transition (April 22 - April 29) at 0.7 bps Retail taker; and a docs commit added the note "As of June 15 Paradex Retail fees go back to 0% for Takers and Makers on all markets." (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://x.com/paradex/status/2036439864443543880 · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/da96460db9fb196d17f08064c9cb35cb971a6de5, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/09b98a847eb0dfb6bebbc79e1f56acc9e4872687, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/d0d175bf506f024c6bb4d4ee0ae232b7fea8b3b4
- [statement] FastFills: a Pro or API order that matches a passive Retail order automatically gets a 30% taker-fee discount (stackable with staking and $DIME discounts, still floored at 1.75 bps (0.0175%)); the fill carries a `fastfill` flag in the List Fills `flags` array. The discount was 75% in a docs commit dated 19 Dec 2025 and 30% in a later docs commit. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/fastfills · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trading-fees, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/276781da90822aa3ec1add322005d8957825b087, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/da96460db9fb196d17f08064c9cb35cb971a6de5, https://api.prod.paradex.trade/v1/orderbook/BTC-USD-PERP/interactive?depth=100
- [statement] Funding is the other cost on a zero-fee venue. Paradex's launch blog says "The only frictions left are spread and funding". Paradex funding is continuous: the rate is recomputed every second, quoted per 8-hour period, and built from a weighted median of impact premiums across several venues (Paradex, Binance, Bybit, OKX, Lighter and Hyperliquid); Hyperfolio's snapshot of 2026-11-10 had BTC at +0.00473%/8h (+5.2% APR) against Hyperliquid's +0.00125%/h (+11.0% APR). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-10) — https://www.paradex.trade/blog/introducing-zero-fee-perps · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/nemanull/arbitrage-observatory/blob/main/docs/profiles/paradex/fees.md, https://www.hyperfolio.fun/en/blog/hyperliquid-vs-paradex-comparison
- [statement] Paradex's public docs source repo carries agents/learnings notes with a 'Last updated' stamp (2026-11-13 on the trading-fees note) that state current rates, for example Pro maker fee for Perps & Spot a flat 0.5 bps (0.005%) as of 2026-11, previously 0.3 bps from July 3, 2026. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/blob/main/agents/learnings/trading-fees.md · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/d0d175bf506f024c6bb4d4ee0ae232b7fea8b3b4, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/226f03c3eec1eb2404c8749fe5cf469b6a8b1bbe, https://api.prod.paradex.trade/v1/system/volume-tiers
- [statement] Current scale is small. DefiLlama shows, as of Nov 22, 2026, Paradex Perp Volume (24h) $4.95m, Open Interest $10.67m, Perp Volume (30d) $241.59m and Weekly Change-54.44%, with $28.82m of perp volume in the last 7 days; CoinGecko shows open_interest_btc 173.55 and trade_volume_24h_btc 70.7; Hyperfolio's snapshot had $3.9M of volume and $25.8M of open interest. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://defillama.com/perps/chain/paradex · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://defillama.com/exchange/paradex/information, https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/derivatives/exchanges/paradex, https://www.hyperfolio.fun/en/blog/hyperliquid-vs-paradex-comparison
- [statement] Published fee numbers about Paradex are often stale or wrong. LiquidView (undated) says Paradex charges 3.5 bps for takers and offers a −0.5 bps rebate for makers; a Binance Square post says Retail taker starts at 0.0075%, paying fees in $DIME gives another 20% and a 1 bps floor applies; Paradex's own blog dated April 2, 2026 says retail pays 0% maker and 0% taker; and FundingView (November 9, 2026) itself says fee tiers have changed several times in 2026, so check the current schedule. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://www.liquidview.app/blog/hyperliquid-vs-paradex · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/318137813106578, https://www.paradex.trade/blog/scalping-fees-shouldnt-kill-your-edge, https://a1research.io/blog/paradex-private-institutional-grade-trading-at-internet-scale, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trading-fees
- [statement] Retail fees have not been 0% without a break. Paradex announced that, effective March 25, 2026, Retail taker fees would be 0.0075%. The docs then moved to Retail volume tiers with a default (VIP 0) taker fee of 0.024% falling to 0.01% at VIP 6, after a one-week transition (April 22 - April 29) at 0.7 bps for Retail takers. A later docs commit says "As of June 15 Paradex Retail fees go back to 0% for Takers and Makers on all markets." (high confidence) — https://www.paradex.trade/blog/introducing-zero-fee-perps · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://x.com/paradex/status/2036439864443543880, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/7951366b09ec6967f8c91d6d3e3b207101d92abd, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/blob/aa6c2b9efc555292eb6327095a823b98759b6868/fern/pages/trading/trading-fees.mdx, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/d0d175bf506f024c6bb4d4ee0ae232b7fea8b3b4
- [statement] The Pro (API) fee schedule in the docs repo changed often. A docs commit of 19 Dec 2025 raised the API maker fee from 0.002% to 0.003% and showed a FastFills discount of 75% to 0.005%. A docs commit of 24 Mar 2026 showed Pro maker 0% effective March 25, 2026, with the FastFills discount at 30% to 0.014%. The docs then added a flat 0.003% (0.3 bps) Pro maker fee effective July 3 at 12:00 SGT, and now show a flat 0.5 bps (0.005%) as of 2026-11. (high confidence) — https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/276781da90822aa3ec1add322005d8957825b087 · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/f3d99c5070d615a82da9984188173b2da870663d, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/20772ee1d712804ee38028841cecf6aabd588f91, https://x.com/paradex/status/2036439864443543880, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/7951366b09ec6967f8c91d6d3e3b207101d92abd
- [statement] Treat the zero fee as revocable. The Paradex blog says the pricing is "not a promo with a countdown" and "There is no end date." The same vendor announced Retail taker fees of 0.0075% effective March 25, 2026, and a later docs commit says "As of June 15 Paradex Retail fees go back to 0% for Takers and Makers on all markets." Design any strategy so that it still works if Retail or Pro fees change. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://www.paradex.trade/blog/scalping-fees-shouldnt-kill-your-edge · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/d0d175bf506f024c6bb4d4ee0ae232b7fea8b3b4, https://x.com/paradex/status/2036439864443543880, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/276781da90822aa3ec1add322005d8957825b087, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/332fbc281b595c664ac5bd5b442517cdf267d632
- [statement] Paradex says Retail stays free because professional market makers pay for Retail flow. Its launch post says makers post RPI orders that are visible in the UI and hidden from the API, pay 0.5 bps on RPI fills, and that high-frequency API takers pay 2 bps (0.02%). Delphi Digital and Alea Research both describe this flow segmentation as payment for order flow. A Blockworks report says Paradex charges market makers between 0.5 and 2.0 bps and Pro API flow 0.3 bps (maker) and 2.0 bps (taker) on perp trades. (medium confidence) — https://www.paradex.trade/blog/introducing-zero-fee-perps · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://members.delphidigital.io/reports/paradex-reimagining-on-chain-markets-from-first-principles, https://alearesearch.substack.com/p/paradex-appchain, https://app.blockworks.com/report/paradex-privacy-first-perp-dex-and-the-dime-tge
- [statement] RPI orders must be Post-Only, have the lowest execution priority at their price level, and match only Retail Taker orders (the matching engine guarantees this). A client places one through the New Order endpoint with `instruction="RPI"`. A Pro order that matches a passive Retail order gets an additional 30% taker fee discount (the 1.75 bps minimum fee still applies). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/rpi · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/fastfills, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trading-fees
- [statement] Hyperfolio's worked examples put the cost of a BTC long (first example) on a Paradex retail order at about 1.16 bps per side (half spread 0.32 bps plus impact 0.84 bps) with $0 in fees. For a HYPE round trip (second example) the Paradex retail book cost about 22.2 bps per side (0 fee + 20.89 bps impact + 1.28 bps half spread) against about 7.3 bps on Hyperliquid (4.5 bps fee + 2.74 bps impact + 0.07 bps half spread). A Pro order through the standard API at Pro 0 pays 0.045% taker into a thinner book, which Hyperfolio found more expensive than Hyperliquid. Hyperfolio discloses that it is funded by Hyperliquid referrals. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-10) — https://www.hyperfolio.fun/en/blog/hyperliquid-vs-paradex-comparison · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trading-fees, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles
- [statement] At 2:53 PM EST the Paradex status page showed UI, Cloud/API, Blockchain, Bridge, Block Explorer and RPC Proxy all Operational at 100% for the last 30 days. This is a vendor self-report. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://status.paradex.trade/ · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API
- [statement] Do not read the vendor's zero-fee marketing as lowest total cost. The Paradex scalping post says that on Paradex, retail now pays 0% maker and 0% taker, "so the same trade returns the full 5.00%", while its FAQ says "Your real cost is fees plus spread plus funding" and that market makers can quote tighter spreads against retail flow. Hyperfolio's snapshot shows a Retail-book BTC spread of 0.63 bps against 0.13 bps on Hyperliquid and Depth ±0.1% of $0.40M against $43.66M. The launch post's self-reported claim of beating top exchanges ~96% of the time on majors at $100k order size covers majors only. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-10) — https://www.paradex.trade/blog/scalping-fees-shouldnt-kill-your-edge · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://www.hyperfolio.fun/en/blog/hyperliquid-vs-paradex-comparison, https://www.paradex.trade/blog/introducing-zero-fee-perps

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] REST rate limits: `POST, DELETE, PUT /orders` 800 req/s OR 17250 req/m per account; `GET /*` 120 req/s OR 600 req/m per account; public default 1500 req/m per IP; private endpoints also share an additional IP-based limit of 1500 req/m across all accounts. A batch order request (`POST /orders/batch`, `DELETE /orders/batch`, 1-50 orders) counts as one rate-limit unit. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/rate-limits/api · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/api-best-practices
- [statement] WebSocket limits: 20 connections per second or 600 connections per minute per IP; order methods (`order.create`, `order.create_batch`, `order.modify`, `order.cancel`, `order.cancel_batch`, `order.cancel_all`) 100 req/s OR 3600 req/m per account, lower than the REST limit. The docs advise batch methods and a separate connection for order entry. Over-limit requests are rejected with error code 42901. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/ws/general-information/rate-limits · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/api-best-practices
- [statement] Pro fee schedule per the current docs: taker 0.045% at Pro 0, 0.042% at Pro 1 (14D volume ≥ 1M), 0.039% at Pro 2 (≥ 5M), 0.037% at Pro 3 (≥ 10M), 0.035% at Pro 4 (≥ 25M); flat Pro maker 0.005% (0.5 bps). Three additive discounts apply to the Pro taker fee: staking $DIME (up to 30%), paying fees in $DIME (40% for all orders during initial rollout) and FastFills (30%). A Pro taker fee cannot go below 1.75 bps (0.0175%). The live volume-tiers endpoint matches: maker 0.00005, taker 0.00045 down to 0.00035 for Pro 0 to Pro 4. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://api.prod.paradex.trade/v1/system/volume-tiers, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/226f03c3eec1eb2404c8749fe5cf469b6a8b1bbe, https://github.com/nemanull/arbitrage-observatory/blob/main/docs/profiles/paradex/fees.md
- [statement] REST rate limits: `POST, DELETE, PUT /orders` 800 req/s OR 17250 req/m per account; `GET /*` 120 req/s OR 600 req/m per account; public endpoints default 1500 req/m per IP (`POST /onboarding` and `POST /auth` 600 req/m); private endpoints also share an extra 1500 req/m limit per IP across all accounts. A batch request (`POST /orders/batch` or `DELETE /orders/batch`, 1-50 orders) counts as one rate-limit unit. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/rate-limits/api · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/api-best-practices
- [statement] WebSocket limits: 20 connections per second or 600 connections per minute per IP; order methods (`order.create`, `order.create_batch`, `order.modify`, `order.cancel`, `order.cancel_batch`, `order.cancel_all`) 100 req/s OR 3600 req/m per account, lower than REST; 10 msg/s and 200 subscriptions per connection. Messages over the message rate are delayed, not rejected, and order requests wait behind them, so use a separate connection for order entry. A client that sends messages faster than the server can process them is disconnected with close code 4032, a connection with no subscriptions for 5 minutes is closed with 4031, an over-limit subscription gets error 42900, and an over-limit order request gets error 42901 despite its "message rate limit exceeded" text. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/ws/general-information/rate-limits · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/blob/main/agents/learnings/websocket-errors-rate-limits.md, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/611fbf4133673333fcb65b87d346c2b15767d00a
- [statement] Paradex's best-practices page advises: sign orders natively (0.4ms C++, 0.2ms Rust average) and pre-sign static order components; use batch order endpoints (a single batch request = 1 rate limit unit regardless of 1-50 orders); pass the optional market parameter on cancel-by-client-id and cancel-all; avoid client IDs when possible; use the bbo.{market_symbol} WebSocket channel for price-only strategies; drain WebSocket messages quickly (the exchange disconnects if 2000+ messages accumulate); synchronize the clock using time.aws.com; and poll GET /v1/system/state, which returns ok, maintenance or cancel_only. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/api-best-practices · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/ws/general-information/rate-limits, https://api.prod.paradex.trade/v1/system/state
- [statement] Credentials for bots: the main private key can withdraw and transfer, so Paradex recommends Subkeys, which can place, cancel and modify orders and access balances and history but cannot withdraw, transfer, modify account settings or manage Subkeys; a Subkey authenticates via `/auth/{public_key}` with the main account address in the `PARADEX-STARKNET-ACCOUNT` header. The official SDK refreshes the JWT 30s before expiry and forwards auth_params such as {"token_usage": "interactive"} on both the initial and the refresh auth calls. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/api-authentication · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-py/blob/main/paradex_py/api/api_client.py, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-py/blob/main/paradex_py/paradex.py
- [statement] The current Paradex fee page lists Retail maker and taker fees at 0% on perps, spot and options, and 0% for RFQ takers. Pro makers on perps and spot pay a flat 0.005% (0.5 bps). Pro takers pay a base rate by 14D volume from 0.045% (Pro 0) to 0.035% (Pro 4, ≥ 25M), per `Your taker fee = base rate × (1 − total discount)`. The discounts add: staking $DIME up to 30%, paying fees in $DIME 40% for all orders during initial rollout, and FastFills 30%. A Pro taker fee cannot go below 1.75 bps (0.0175%). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/226f03c3eec1eb2404c8749fe5cf469b6a8b1bbe
- [statement] The WebSocket rate-limit page lists a separate Retail limit: 10 req/s OR 10 req/m OR 100 req/h OR 2000 req/24h per account on `order.create`, `order.create_batch` and `order.modify`, in addition to 100 req/s OR 3600 req/m for all order methods. The docs also say order requests sent through the REST API count toward this limit. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/ws/general-information/rate-limits · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/blob/main/agents/learnings/websocket-errors-rate-limits.md, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/611fbf4133673333fcb65b87d346c2b15767d00a
- [statement] Paradex REST limits: `POST, DELETE, PUT /orders` 800 req/s OR 17250 req/m per account; `GET /*` 120 req/s OR 600 req/m per account; public endpoints 1500 req/m per IP; private endpoints also share an additional 1500 req/m IP limit across accounts. One batch request (`POST /orders/batch` or `DELETE /orders/batch`, 1-50 orders) costs one unit. WebSocket: 100 req/s OR 3600 req/m per account for order methods with no IP based limit, 10 msg/s and 200 subscriptions per connection. Messages over the message rate are delayed, a client that sends messages faster than the server can process them is disconnected with close code 4032, and an over-limit order request is rejected with error code 42901. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/rate-limits/api · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/ws/general-information/rate-limits, https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/api-best-practices

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] If an account exceeds the Retail rate limits it automatically switches to Pro Order behavior and loses access to RPI liquidity; over WebSocket a Retail order over its limit is rejected rather than switched to Pro Order behavior. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/ws/general-information/rate-limits
- [statement] Over-limit behavior differs by channel. On REST, a Retail account that exceeds the Retail limits automatically switches to Pro Order behavior and loses access to RPI liquidity. On WebSocket, Retail order.create, order.create_batch and order.modify carry an extra per-account limit (10 req/s OR 10 req/m OR 100 req/h OR 2000 req/24h) and an over-limit order is rejected rather than switched to Pro Order behavior. REST order requests also count toward the WebSocket order limit, and a batch request counts as one request. A request over the limit is rejected with error code 42901. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/ws/general-information/rate-limits, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/blob/main/agents/learnings/websocket-errors-rate-limits.md, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/611fbf4133673333fcb65b87d346c2b15767d00a
- [statement] Paradex says it funds zero retail fees from RPI (Retail Price Improvement) maker flow rather than from retail takers: professional makers post RPI orders that are visible in the UI and hidden from the API, they match only retail takers, and makers pay 0.5 bps on RPI fills; the launch blog added that high-frequency API takers pay 2 bps and that toxicity-based fees would follow. Delphi Digital and Alea Research independently describe this flow segmentation as payment for order flow (PFOF). DefiLlama's protocol page lists Fees 30d of $33,929 and Perp Volume 30d of $241.59m. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://www.paradex.trade/blog/introducing-zero-fee-perps · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://members.delphidigital.io/reports/paradex-reimagining-on-chain-markets-from-first-principles, https://alearesearch.substack.com/p/paradex-appchain, https://defillama.com/protocol/paradex
- [statement] Retail orders carry a 300ms speed bump on submission and on cancellation. The Retail limits are 3 orders / sec, 30 orders / min, 300 orders / hr and 1,000 orders / 24 hrs, against 800 orders / sec and 17,250 orders / min for Pro. An account that exceeds the Retail limits switches to Pro Order behavior and loses access to RPI liquidity. Over WebSocket a Retail Order over its limit is rejected rather than switched to Pro Order behavior, with error code 42901. A docs commit of 30 Oct 2025 raised the retail activity thresholds from 10 orders / minute, 60 orders / hour and 750 orders / 24 hours to 30 orders / minute, 300 orders / hour and 1000 orders / 24 hours. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/ws/general-information/rate-limits, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/065e93dd274b1352dd4ea6fe51ba9d375bbccbef, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/53388a63ab02b88ef757c742fa4bb9edea5504ce

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The zero fee applies to the order, not to the account: Paradex classifies each order as Retail or Pro by how it is submitted. UI orders and API orders sent with a JWT obtained via `token_usage=interactive` are Retail; API orders with a standard JWT are Pro by default and use the Pro fee schedule. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/rpi
- [statement] Pro traders pay volume-tiered taker fees that they can reduce by staking $DIME or paying fees in $DIME. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://www.paradex.trade/blog/scalping-fees-shouldnt-kill-your-edge
- [statement] During a planned 30-minute database upgrade, a race condition caused corrupted market data to be written onchain and triggered unintended liquidations across multiple markets. Paradex rolled Paradex Chain back to block 1604710, cancelled open orders except take-profit and stop-loss orders, and refunded $650,000 to about 200 users. It marked the first rollback of the chain, and added updated restart procedures, data validation checks and price-band protections during post-only trading periods. (high confidence) — https://www.tradingview.com/news/cointelegraph:7fc5cadc0094b:0-paradex-refunds-650k-to-200-users-after-maintenance-bug-triggers-liquidations/ · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://www.dlnews.com/articles/defi/paradex-announces-rollback-after-perp-exchange-users-report-mass-liquidations/
- [statement] The zero fee attaches to each order, not to the account. Orders placed in the Paradex UI, and API orders sent with a JWT requested using the `token_usage=interactive` query parameter, are Retail orders; API orders without an interactive token are Pro by default. Paradex's Python SDK docstring for auth_params gives {"token_usage": "interactive"} as its example "for 0-fee JWT", its twap_order.py example defaults to interactive auth to obtain a "0-fee JWT token", and a third-party Rust client also exposes optional `token_usage=interactive`. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-py/blob/main/paradex_py/paradex.py, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-py/blob/main/examples/twap_order.py, https://github.com/calumrussell/roshar/blob/main/roshar-paradex/README.md
- [statement] Perp market count: Zero Fee Perps launched on 100+ perps; CoinGecko counts 66 perpetual pairs, and a third-party probe retrieved 2026-10-12 found 66 USD-quoted perpetuals of which 23 were tagged RWA. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/derivatives/exchanges/paradex · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://defillama.com/exchange/paradex/information, https://github.com/nemanull/arbitrage-observatory/blob/main/docs/profiles/paradex/fees.md, https://www.paradex.trade/blog/introducing-zero-fee-perps
- [statement] Paradex's Restricted Persons page lists US persons and Canadian persons as Restricted Persons and Canada and the United States as restricted territories (plus sanctioned persons and regions), and says none of them are eligible to use Paradex's products and services, so zero-fee retail access is not open to them. A third-party probe found no location check in the public API from a Canadian exit, which is not the same as permission to trade. US-person access is owned by a sibling concept. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://www.paradex.trade/restricted-persons · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://www.paradex.trade/terms-of-service, https://github.com/nemanull/arbitrage-observatory/blob/main/docs/profiles/paradex/fees.md
- [statement] RPI orders are Post-Only maker orders placed on the New Order endpoint with `instruction="RPI"`. The matching engine guarantees they match only Retail Taker orders (orders submitted with an interactive JWT token), never regular API orders; they have the lowest execution priority at their price level, they rest until cancelled even away from the BBO, and they are absent from the API order book, so the UI book can look crossed while the API book stays uncrossed. Delphi's report called RPI a UI-only price-improvement lane; the docs now also count interactive-token API orders as Retail takers. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/rpi · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://members.delphidigital.io/reports/paradex-reimagining-on-chain-markets-from-first-principles, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles
- [statement] The Retail-visible book is available over the API: `GET /v1/bbo/{market}/interactive` and `GET /v1/orderbook/{market}/interactive`; the interactive book is what Retail orders see and includes RPI quotes. The orderbook endpoint also carries best_bid_interactive, best_ask_interactive, best_bid_api and best_ask_api size fields. A third-party Rust client lists both interactive endpoints. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://github.com/calumrussell/roshar/blob/main/roshar-paradex/README.md · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/blob/master/ts/src/paradex.ts, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/fastfills, https://api.prod.paradex.trade/v1/orderbook/BTC-USD-PERP/interactive?depth=100
- [statement] Tooling: the auth docs list paradex-py and paradex-js as SDKs and the best-practices page links a C++ Starknet signing library; third parties include the Rust roshar-paradex client (SBE decoding of websocket payloads, Stark-curve signing, authenticated REST trading) and the sv/mcp-paradex-py MCP server, whose repository was archived by its owner on Jun 18, 2026 and is read-only. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/api-authentication · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/api-best-practices, https://github.com/calumrussell/roshar/blob/main/roshar-paradex/README.md, https://github.com/sv/mcp-paradex-py
- [statement] During recovery from the Jan 2026 incident the platform ran in CANCEL_ONLY and then POST_ONLY mode before reopening, and Paradex then added post-only period price band protection. Bots should poll GET /v1/system/state (ok, maintenance, cancel_only), halt new order submissions during cancel_only while continuing cancellations, and expect aggressive orders in a post-only period to skew the mark price. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://status.paradex.trade/posts/details/PVQ05Y4 · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/api-best-practices, https://api.prod.paradex.trade/v1/system/state, https://x.com/paradex/status/2014616141508051376
- [statement] Volume has fallen sharply from its January 2026 levels. DL News cited almost $1.6 billion of trades the day before the incident; A1 Research cited over $1.2 billion daily with $751 million in open interest (January 13, 2026); Stork says average daily volume went $68M → $2.1B during its Season 2 rewards program, which concluded in January 2026. DefiLlama shows, as of Nov 22, 2026, perp volume on Paradex of $4.95m in the last 24 hours. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://www.dlnews.com/articles/defi/paradex-announces-rollback-after-perp-exchange-users-report-mass-liquidations/ · keywords: Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/01/19/paradex-rolls-back-blockchain-after-data-glitch-valuing-bitcoin-at-usd0-triggers-mass-liquidations, https://a1research.io/blog/paradex-private-institutional-grade-trading-at-internet-scale, https://www.stork.network/case-studies/perp-dex-oracle-paradex, https://defillama.com/perps/chain/paradex
- [statement] Incident timeline from the status page (Jan 19, 2026, EST): 12:36 AM investigating; 1:51 AM rollback to block 1604710 announced; 3:03 AM all open orders force cancelled except TPSL orders; 5:16 AM "all user funds are SAFU" with no confirmed ETA; 5:52 AM CANCEL_ONLY; 6:50 AM POST_ONLY; 7:15 AM "Paradex is back online". CoinDesk reported that Paradex came back online at 12:10 UTC after around eight hours of downtime. ## Source disagreement — Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API

Press framing of the Jan 2026 incident differs from the post-mortem: CoinDesk and DL News reported that bitcoin's (and other) prices fell to zero on Paradex, while Paradex's post-mortem attributes the liquidations to funding indexes reset to 0 in some markets and does not mention zero prices.
